title: Draft: dfilter: Try the set true_false_string before the default
description:
When making an fvalue from a string, try the value string matching
before string matching. This only affects FT_BOOLEAN, which matches
on string literals "True" and "False" as a fallback. In particular,
this affects any boolean field that uses the strings "True" or "False"
to mean the opposite of their normal meanings. (Ed.: Fields should
avoid doing that, it's confusing. `flexray.nfi` should use something
else like { "Null", "Not Null" }.)

This also changes the error message when matching integer types against
strings and there's no strings - it produces an error about not having
a value string instead of a generic error about not being able to
convert from a string. Change one of the tests to reflect this.

Don't change the behavior and order when converting from a literal -
matching value strings with unquoted literals is deprecated, so it
should be tried last (and continue not to override previous error
messages.)

Note that this makes `flexray.nfi == True` be different than
`flexray.nfi == "True"`, which is the price of having a misleading
true_false_string. The unquoted literal True *always* matches 1;
that's true for all the other true_false_strings that have a negative
connotation for 1/true as well. As noted, to use the value from the
value string it should be quoted.

Fix #20262

notes.body: I'm not sure it's easy to make this work with the edge case of `FT_BOOLEAN` fields that share the same abbreviation but having different `true_false_strings`. Perhaps it simply shouldn't be allowed to register a field with a `true_false_string` with "True" or "False" in it (particularly reversed.)

changes_data.diff:
@@ -100,7 +100,7 @@ class TestDfilterMembership:
 
     def test_membership_11_bad_rhs_string(self, checkDFilterFail):
         dfilter = 'frame.number in {1, "foo"}'
-        error = 'Unsigned integer (32 bits) cannot be converted from a string'
+        error = 'frame.number cannot accept strings as values.'
         checkDFilterFail(dfilter, error)
 
     def test_membership_12_value_string(self, checkDFilterCount):
